intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 27 October 2026 comprised three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 have been reported as Easy‑to‑Moderate overall, with Shift 1 leaning slightly easier and Shift 2 described as Moderate, though candidate opinions vary. The Quantitative sections were noted as the most challenging in both reported shifts, while Reasoning, General Awareness and English showed mixed difficulty levels. Figures such as the range of good attempts are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts. No usable analysis is published yet for Shift 3, and further candidate evidence is required before a review can be posted.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shifts 1 and 2 were reported as Easy‑to‑Moderate overall, with Shift 1 described as Easy to Moderate and Shift 2 as Moderate (reports differ). Shift 3 has no published analysis yet.

faqs.q: How did the Quantitative sections compare across the shifts on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: In both reported shifts (1 and 2), the Quantitative section was identified as the toughest part of the paper, featuring advanced calculations and a tight time limit. No quantitative analysis is available for Shift 3 at this time.

faqs.q: What does the reported range of good attempts indicate for the 27 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: The unofficial ranges suggest that candidates who attempted between 20–78 questions performed well in Shift 1, while in Shift 2 the range was roughly 65–88 across sections. These numbers are not official and should be interpreted cautiously.

faqs.q: Is there any analysis available for Shift 3 of the 27 October 2026 Tier 1 paper?
faqs.a: No usable analysis has been published for Shift 3 yet. A review will be added once sufficient candidate evidence is gathered.

faqs.q: How does SSC handle score normalization across the different shifts on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure fairness, meaning that raw marks from each shift are adjusted to a common scale before final ranking.
